mistake_reason: Tool Output Misinterpretation (FM-4.2): At step 18 (0-indexed 19th message), the orchestrator incorrectly interpreted the WebSurfer’s structured extraction, which explicitly stated that “A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984)” was credited with popularizing the metaleptic crossing between dream world and reality, while “Friday the 13th (1980)” was a slasher example unrelated to that concept. Despite multiple clear tool outputs (quotes and a structured mapping) pointing to “A Nightmare on Elm Street,” the orchestrator misread the list (apparently treating the first listed item as the answer and ignoring the 'unrelated' label) and concluded the cited film was “Friday the 13th.” This is a direct misinterpretation of accurate tool outputs. Later, at step 24-25, the orchestrator further misinterpreted term frequency counts (and ignored a warning that counts do not imply prominence) as supporting evidence, compounding the FM-4.2 error.
